Wasserstein / Transport-Scale Proportion Mediated

Source: R/wasserstein-pmed.R
wasserstein_pmed.Rd

Estimate P_med^W = NIE^W / (NIE^W + NDE^W), the transport-scale proportion mediated, where NIE^W = W_2(nu_11, nu_10) and NDE^W = W_2(nu_10, nu_00) are the 2-Wasserstein distances between the corner laws nu(a, a').

Three estimation methods are available:

  • "eif" (default): deterministic parametric g-computation with an observed-row influence-function SE. Includes both fitted-model and empirical covariate-distribution uncertainty. Requires correct working models, iid rows, full-rank fits, and nonzero components; d = 1 only. The legacy name does not assert nonparametric efficiency.

  • "bootstrap": row bootstrap refitting the same deterministic estimator. Used automatically near either zero-component boundary. Boundary coverage is not guaranteed by this fallback.

  • "dr": cross-fit DR corner-CDF estimator (multiply robust: consistent when either the outcome or propensity model is wrong, mediator model correct) with bootstrap SE. Slowest; d = 1 only.

Usage

wasserstein_pmed(
  object,
  covars = "C",
  n_mc = 20000L,
  binY = FALSE,
  method = c("eif", "bootstrap", "dr"),
  n_boot = 200L,
  K = 5L,
  G = 300L,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  seed = 1L,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A data.frame with columns A (binary 0/1), M (mediator), Y (outcome), and the covariates named in covars.

covars

Character vector of covariate column names. Default "C".

n_mc

Legacy compatibility argument (default 20000), now ignored. G-computation uses deterministic quadrature instead of simulated corner laws.

binY

Logical: if TRUE, treats Y as binary (uses logistic g-comp).

method

Character: "eif" (default), "bootstrap", or "dr".

n_boot

Integer: bootstrap replications (default 200). Used by "bootstrap" and "dr" methods, and automatically when near the boundary.

K

Integer: cross-fitting folds for method = "dr" (default 5).

G

Integer: y-grid points for method = "dr" (default 300).

ci_level

Numeric: confidence level (default 0.95).

seed

Integer: RNG seed (default 1).

...

Unused.

Value

A WassersteinPmedResult object.

Details

The g-computation methods assume a homoscedastic Gaussian mediator model M ~ A + covars and an outcome model Y ~ A * M + covars (homoscedastic Gaussian, or Bernoulli-logit when binY = TRUE). Covariates are standardized over the observed rows. Residual variances use mean squared residuals, not degrees-of-freedom corrections. Gaussian outcomes use 128-point quadrature over mixture quantiles; binary outcomes use 64-point normal quadrature. These are numerical approximations, not certified error bounds. Wald inference is model-based and requires regular, nonzero distance components; it is not a method for clustered observations or unsupported outcome families.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 800; C <- rnorm(n)
A <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(0.3 * C))
M <- 0.7 * A + 0.5 * C + rnorm(n)
Y <- 0.6 * A + 0.8 * M + 0.3 * C + rnorm(n)
wasserstein_pmed(data.frame(A, M, Y, C), covars = "C")
#> Wasserstein P_med^W (eif, n=800)
#>   P_med^W = 0.440  [0.345, 0.535]  (se=0.048)
#>   NIE^W=0.525  NDE^W=0.668  TE^W=1.193  G^W(synergy)=0.000
